creator: Haoyu Zhang, Lifang Zhou, Yifan Jin, Yuexiu Yuan, Leyuan Zhang, Jiahan Li, Xinying Jing, Xingang Sang, Qianqian Yu
description: Background and objectivesPrimary care physicians face substantial occupational mental health challenges, including job burnout and turnover intention. Psychological contract theory conceptualizes employment relationships in terms of perceived reciprocal obligations, while the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model provides a complementary framework for understanding how work-related conditions may be associated with burnout.

title: Development and external validation of an explainable XGBoost model with a web-based calculator for risk prediction of postpartum depressive symptoms
creator: Qian Zhang, Fang Wu, Mei Zhu, Liwei Sun
description: IntroductionPostpartum depression (PPD) is associated with severe adverse outcomes, yet timely risk stratification remains challenging. Existing machine learning models are often limited by insufficient external validation, limited interpretability, and lack of accessible clinical tools. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an explainable machine learning model with a web-based calculator for predicting postpartum depressive symptoms.

title: Highlighting person-centredness in technology supported care within nursing homes: a multiple case study
creator: A. C. Noordam, C. J. Nierse, R. J. E. Vugs, V. T. J. Bisschops, J. Adriaansen, T. J. van der Zijpp, S. Cardiff
description: Healthcare technologies are increasingly introduced in long-term care to support monitoring, assessment and clinical decision-making. In nursing homes, however, their use becomes intertwined with everyday care practices and relationships between professionals, residents and family members. This study explores how digital health technologies shape care relationships in nursing homes from a person-centred care perspective.

title: Lung microbial dysregulation and TNF inhibition are associated with worsened nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease
creator: Ethan G. Napier, Isaac R. Cinco, Delphine C. Malherbe, Ethan V. Stuart, Michael H. Davies, Caroline N. Leach, Evan Damron, Mahmut Gokmen, Amy Leestemaker-Palmer, Stephanie Nuss, Cody Bumgardner, Steven G. Kohama, Luiz Bermudez, Kevin L. Winthrop, Cristina Fuss, Eliot R. Spindel, Ilhem Messaoudi
description: IntroductionNontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are ubiquitous bacteria that cause a spectrum of diseases, most notably pulmonary disease (NTMPD). The host factors contributing to the heightened susceptibility and severity of NTMPD in elderly individuals are poorly understood. Prior studies have reported increased incidence of NTMPD in individuals receiving immune modulatory biologics such as anti-TNF and JAK-STAT inhibitors.

title: Recycling mushroom residue as a soil amendment: pH-associated attenuation of blueberry crown gall severity diverging from enhanced rhizosphere denitrification
creator: Liu Hong, Zhang Tianlun
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cold region blueberry production faces constraints from unsuitable soils and crown gall disease caused by Agrobacterium tumefaciens. To investigate whether amendment-mediated soil changes regulate this disease, a 3 × 3 factorial pot experiment was conducted with three amendments [CK (none), T1 (peat + sulfur), and T2 (peat + mushroom residue + sulfur)] under three water regimes, using artificial stem-wound inoculation with A.

title: Glucose and insulin dynamics following low-carbohydrate and low-fat diets in females with lipedema and obesity
creator: Julianne Lundanes, Anne Sofie Fischer, Simon Nitter Dankel, Jens Juul Holst, Catia Martins, Siren Nymo
description: IntroductionLow-carbohydrate diets (LCDs) have been suggested as a potential treatment option for females with lipedema, due to their superiority in reducing pain, possibly through improvements in insulin dynamics.ObjectivesThe objective of this secondary analysis was to compare changes in markers of glucose and insulin dynamics after a low-carbohydrate versus low-fat low-energy diets in females with lipedema and obesity.

title: Alcalase-hydrolyzed casein peptides after simulated gastrointestinal digestion alleviate high-fat diet-induced metabolic dysfunction in mice
creator: Ling Mo, Chaochao Zhao, Tian Wang, Wanli Xu, Yingping Deng, Yongming Yu, Xiaoyun Zeng
description: Background and aimHigh-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic dysfunction is associated with disturbances in gut microbial composition and hepatic lipid metabolism. This study investigated the metabolic effects of Alcalase-hydrolyzed casein peptides after simulated gastrointestinal digestion (MCPs) in HFD-fed mice and explored their potential association with gut microbiota and fecal metabolic alterations.

title: An upstream approach to veterinary workforce wellbeing: an evaluative review of an embedded wellbeing curriculum in veterinary education
creator: Virginia K. Corrigan, Jennifer Carter, Rachel H. Colla, Laura Dooley, Lara H. Mossman, Dianne A. Vella-Brodrick
description: Veterinary professionals work in demanding environments shaped by individual, relational, organizational, and systemic pressures. Veterinary education can therefore serve as an upstream setting for developing both clinical competence and the capabilities needed for sustainable professional engagement and wellbeing. Competency-based veterinary education offers a structure for treating wellbeing as a professional capability that can be taught, practiced, assessed, and evaluated.

title: Imeglimin may improve albuminuria associated with partial suppression of inflammatory and fibrotic markers in diabetic kidney disease
creator: Yoshimi Muta, Hisashi Yokomizo, Takako Kawanami, Yuriko Hamaguchi, Dai Nagata, Mayuko Yamamoto, Yuki Senda, Yuichi Takashi, Shohta Kodama, Daiji Kawanami
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Imeglimin is an oral hypoglycemic agent marketed in Japan that has shown glucose-lowering effects in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes in TIMES trials. However, it is not well known whether imeglimin can affect diabetic kidney disease (DKD). To clarify this, we investigated the potential association between the effects of imeglimin and DKD using diabetic mice (DM) and cultured endothelial cells. Administration of imeglimin significantly lowered urinary albumin excretion in DKD but did not significantly affect blood glucose and glycated albumin.
